questionText: The word 'refuse' has two meanings. Which sentence uses it to mean 'garbage'?
options: A) The refuse was collected on Monday.
B) She refuse to leave.
C) They will refuse permission.
D) He will not refuse the offer.
explanation: Refuse (REF-yoos) means garbage or waste - R-E-F-U-S-E. Refuse (re-FYOOZ) means to decline.

questionText: How is the word 'content' pronounced in 'She was content with her grade'?
options: A) con-TENT (adjective meaning satisfied)
B) CON-tent (noun meaning information)
C) con-tent (adverb)
D) CON-TENT (both syllables stressed)
explanation: Content as an adjective means satisfied - con-TENT. Content as a noun means information or subject matter - CON-tent.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'wound' to mean an injury?
options: A) She had a wound on her arm.
B) He wound the rope around the pole.
C) She wound up the clock.
D) The path wound through the forest.
explanation: Wound (WOOND) means an injury - W-O-U-N-D. Wound (WOWND) is the past tense of wind meaning to turn.

questionText: The word 'lead' can mean a metal or to guide. Which sentence uses it as a metal?
options: A) The pipe was made of lead.
B) She will lead the team.
C) Please lead the way.
D) He tried to lead by example.
explanation: Lead (LED) is the heavy metal - L-E-A-D. Lead (LEED) means to guide or show the way.

questionText: How is 'present' pronounced when it means a gift?
options: A) PREZ-ent (noun)
B) pre-ZENT (verb)
C) PREE-zent
D) preh-SENT
explanation: Present as a noun (gift or attendance) is stressed on the first syllable - PREZ-ent. Present as a verb is stressed on the second - pre-ZENT.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'row' pronounced to rhyme with 'go'?
options: A) We sat in the front row.
B) They had a terrible row.
C) The row between them was loud.
D) She reported the row to the teacher.
explanation: Row (rhymes with go) means a line - R-O-W. Row (rhymes with cow) means a noisy argument.

questionText: The word 'tear' has two pronunciations. Which sentence uses it to mean to rip?
options: A) She will tear the paper.
B) A tear fell down his cheek.
C) She wiped a tear from her eye.
D) He felt a tear of sadness.
explanation: Tear (rhymes with bear) means to rip - T-E-A-R. Tear (rhymes with ear) means a drop of water from the eye.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'minute' to mean very small?
options: A) The difference was minute.
B) Wait one minute please.
C) The meeting lasted a minute.
D) It is five minutes away.
explanation: Minute (my-NYOOT) means very small or tiny - M-I-N-U-T-E. Minute (MIN-it) means 60 seconds.

questionText: The word 'object' can be a noun or a verb. Which sentence uses it as a verb?
options: A) She will object to the decision.
B) What is that object on the table?
C) The object was found in the room.
D) He placed the object carefully.
explanation: Object as a verb (ob-JECT) means to express disagreement - O-B-J-E-C-T. As a noun (OB-ject), it means a thing.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'dove' pronounced to rhyme with 'love'?
options: A) A dove sat on the branch.
B) He dove into the pool.
C) She dove for cover.
D) They dove deep into the subject.
explanation: Dove (rhymes with love) is a type of bird - D-O-V-E. Dove (rhymes with stove) is the past tense of dive.

questionText: The word 'desert' can mean to abandon or a dry region. Which meaning applies to: 'The soldiers deserted the camp'?
options: A) To abandon
B) A dry region
C) A sweet food
D) A barren place
explanation: Desert (de-ZERT) means to abandon - D-E-S-E-R-T. Desert (DEZ-ert) means a dry, barren land.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'permit' as a noun?
options: A) She obtained a parking permit.
B) I will permit you to leave.
C) They will not permit smoking.
D) Please permit me to explain.
explanation: Permit (PER-mit) as a noun means an official document - P-E-R-M-I-T. Permit (per-MIT) as a verb means to allow.

questionText: The word 'bass' has two pronunciations. Which sentence uses it to mean a musical instrument?
options: A) He played bass guitar in the band.
B) They caught a bass in the river.
C) The bass was difficult to reel in.
D) She fried the bass for dinner.
explanation: Bass (BAYSS) means a low musical frequency - B-A-S-S. Bass (rhymes with class) is a type of fish.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'close' pronounced to rhyme with 'nose'?
options: A) She was close to winning.
B) Please close the door.
C) Close the window now.
D) He closed his eyes slowly.
explanation: Close (rhymes with nose) means near - C-L-O-S-E. Close (rhymes with doze) means to shut.

questionText: The word 'record' changes stress depending on its function. How is it stressed as a noun?
options: A) REC-ord (first syllable)
B) re-CORD (second syllable)
C) REC-ORD (both syllables)
D) rec-ord (unstressed)
explanation: Record as a noun stresses the first syllable - REC-ord. Record as a verb stresses the second - re-CORD.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'console' as a verb?
options: A) She tried to console him after the loss.
B) He sat at the game console.
C) The console had many buttons.
D) She bought a new gaming console.
explanation: Console (con-SOLE) as a verb means to comfort - C-O-N-S-O-L-E. Console (CON-sole) as a noun is a panel of controls.

questionText: The word 'incense' has two meanings. Which sentence uses it to mean to make angry?
options: A) The injustice incensed the crowd.
B) She lit incense in the temple.
C) The scent of incense filled the room.
D) They burned incense at the ceremony.
explanation: Incense (in-SENSE) as a verb means to make very angry - I-N-C-E-N-S-E. Incense (IN-sense) as a noun is a fragrant substance.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'wind' to mean moving air?
options: A) A strong wind blew the leaves.
B) Please wind the clock.
C) The path will wind through the hills.
D) She wound the thread carefully.
explanation: Wind (rhymes with sinned) means moving air - W-I-N-D. Wind (rhymes with find) means to turn or coil.

questionText: The word 'project' changes stress when used as a noun versus a verb. How is it stressed as a noun?
options: A) PROJ-ect
B) pro-JECT
C) PROJ-ECT
D) pro-ject
explanation: Project as a noun stresses the first syllable - PROJ-ect. Project as a verb stresses the second - pro-JECT.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'bow' pronounced to rhyme with 'cow'?
options: A) She took a bow after the performance.
B) He wore a bow tie.
C) She shot an arrow from the bow.
D) The bow of the ship was decorated.
explanation: Bow (rhymes with cow) means to bend the body - B-O-W. Bow (rhymes with show) means a tied ribbon or archery equipment.

questionText: The word 'upset' can be an adjective, noun, or verb. Which sentence uses it as a verb?
options: A) Do not upset the balance.
B) She was feeling very upset.
C) It caused a major upset.
D) He was upset by the news.
explanation: Upset as a verb means to disturb or overturn - U-P-S-E-T. As an adjective it means emotionally disturbed.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'conduct' as a noun?
options: A) His conduct was praised.
B) She will conduct the orchestra.
C) He will conduct an experiment.
D) They conduct training sessions.
explanation: Conduct (CON-duct) as a noun means behavior - C-O-N-D-U-C-T. Conduct (con-DUCT) as a verb means to direct or carry out.

questionText: The word 'number' can mean a numeral or more numb. Which is the heteronym meaning more numb?
options: A) My fingers grew number in the cold.
B) What is your number?
C) Give me a number.
D) Pick a number between one and ten.
explanation: Number (NUM-mer) as a comparative adjective means more numb - N-U-M-B-E-R. Number as a noun refers to a numeral.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'protest' as a noun?
options: A) They staged a protest.
B) She will protest the decision.
C) He chose to protest loudly.
D) They will protest the new law.
explanation: Protest (PRO-test) as a noun means a public demonstration - P-R-O-T-E-S-T. Protest (pro-TEST) as a verb means to object to.

questionText: The word 'graduate' can be used as both a noun and a verb. Which sentence uses it as a verb?
options: A) She will graduate this year.
B) He is a graduate of that school.
C) The graduate received a medal.
D) She is the top graduate.
explanation: Graduate (GRAD-yoo-ate) as a verb means to complete a degree - G-R-A-D-U-A-T-E. As a noun (GRAD-yoo-it) it means one who has completed studies.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'deliberate' as an adjective?
options: A) It was a deliberate mistake.
B) The jury will deliberate.
C) They began to deliberate the case.
D) She deliberated for a long time.
explanation: Deliberate (de-LIB-er-it) as an adjective means intentional - D-E-L-I-B-E-R-A-T-E. Deliberate (de-LIB-er-ate) as a verb means to consider carefully.

questionText: The word 'intimate' changes meaning and pronunciation. Which sentence uses it as a verb?
options: A) She will intimate her decision soon.
B) They are intimate friends.
C) He shared intimate details.
D) This is an intimate gathering.
explanation: Intimate (IN-ti-mate) as a verb means to imply or make known - I-N-T-I-M-A-T-E. As an adjective (IN-ti-mit) it means close or personal.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'compact' as a noun?
options: A) She carried a compact in her bag.
B) The data was stored in compact form.
C) They live in a compact apartment.
D) The compact car saves fuel.
explanation: Compact (COM-pact) as a noun is a small case for powder and mirror - C-O-M-P-A-C-T. Compact (com-PACT) as an adjective means small and dense.

questionText: The word 'contract' changes stress when used as a noun versus verb. How is it stressed as a verb?
options: A) con-TRACT
B) CON-tract
C) CON-TRACT
D) con-tract
explanation: Contract as a verb stresses the second syllable - con-TRACT. It means to make smaller or to enter into an agreement.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'subject' as a verb?
options: A) The prisoners were subjected to harsh treatment.
B) History is her favourite subject.
C) He chose science as his subject.
D) Change the subject of the sentence.
explanation: Subject (sub-JECT) as a verb means to cause to undergo - S-U-B-J-E-C-T. Subject (SUB-ject) as a noun means a topic or person.

questionText: The word 'perfect' changes stress. How is it stressed as a verb?
options: A) per-FECT
B) PER-fect
C) PER-FECT
D) per-fect
explanation: Perfect as a verb stresses the second syllable - per-FECT. It means to make perfect or complete. As an adjective it is PER-fect.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'escort' as a noun?
options: A) The diplomat had a security escort.
B) He will escort her to the event.
C) Police will escort the dignitary.
D) She asked them to escort the visitors.
explanation: Escort (ES-cort) as a noun is a person who accompanies another - E-S-C-O-R-T. Escort (es-CORT) as a verb means to accompany.

questionText: The word 'compound' can be a noun, adjective, or verb. Which sentence uses it as a verb?
options: A) The problems compounded over time.
B) She lives in a large compound.
C) It is a compound fracture.
D) They entered the compound gates.
explanation: Compound (com-POUND) as a verb means to make worse - C-O-M-P-O-U-N-D. As a noun (COM-pound) it means an enclosed area.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'discount' as a verb?
options: A) Do not discount his idea.
B) She received a large discount.
C) The shop offered a discount.
D) There was a ten percent discount.
explanation: Discount (dis-COUNT) as a verb means to dismiss or reduce - D-I-S-C-O-U-N-T. As a noun (DIS-count) it means a price reduction.

questionText: The word 'rebel' changes stress depending on usage. Which sentence uses it as a noun?
options: A) He was known as a rebel.
B) She will rebel against authority.
C) They chose to rebel.
D) The citizens rebelled against the king.
explanation: Rebel (REB-el) as a noun means a person who resists authority - R-E-B-E-L. Rebel (re-BEL) as a verb means to resist.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'abstract' as a verb?
options: A) Please abstract the key points from the report.
B) She enjoys abstract art.
C) The painting is very abstract.
D) He submitted an abstract for the conference.
explanation: Abstract (ab-STRACT) as a verb means to extract key information - A-B-S-T-R-A-C-T. As a noun or adjective (AB-stract), it refers to something conceptual.

questionText: The word 'entrance' can mean to fill with wonder or a doorway. Which sentence uses it to mean to enchant?
options: A) Her singing entranced the audience.
B) Use the main entrance.
C) The entrance is on the left.
D) He walked through the entrance.
explanation: Entrance (en-TRANCE) as a verb means to fill with delight - E-N-T-R-A-N-C-E. Entrance (EN-trance) as a noun means a doorway.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'buffet' as a verb?
options: A) The waves buffeted the boat.
B) She enjoyed the hotel buffet.
C) The buffet had many dishes.
D) They served lunch as a buffet.
explanation: Buffet (BUF-fet) as a verb means to strike repeatedly - B-U-F-F-E-T. Buffet (boo-FAY) as a noun is a self-service meal.

questionText: The word 'primer' has two pronunciations. Which meaning uses the pronunciation PRIM-er?
options: A) An introductory book
B) A coat of paint
C) An explosive device
D) A beginning lesson
explanation: Primer (PRIM-er) refers to an introductory book - P-R-I-M-E-R. Primer (PRY-mer) refers to a first coat of paint or a detonator.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'moderate' as a verb?
options: A) She will moderate the debate.
B) He held moderate views.
C) The weather is moderate today.
D) She had a moderate reaction.
explanation: Moderate (MOD-er-ate) as a verb means to chair or control - M-O-D-E-R-A-T-E. Moderate (MOD-er-it) as an adjective means average or not extreme.

questionText: The word 'delegate' changes usage. Which sentence uses it as a verb?
options: A) She decided to delegate the task.
B) He is a delegate to the conference.
C) The delegate spoke first.
D) Each country sent a delegate.
explanation: Delegate (DEL-e-gate) as a verb means to assign - D-E-L-E-G-A-T-E. Delegate (DEL-e-git) as a noun means a representative.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'attribute' as a noun?
options: A) Patience is her greatest attribute.
B) We can attribute success to hard work.
C) She will attribute the error to fatigue.
D) They attribute the win to teamwork.
explanation: Attribute (AT-trib-yoot) as a noun means a quality or characteristic - A-T-T-R-I-B-U-T-E. Attribute (at-TRIB-yoot) as a verb means to ascribe or credit.

questionText: The word 'digest' changes stress. How is it stressed as a noun?
options: A) DI-gest
B) di-GEST
C) DI-GEST
D) di-gest
explanation: Digest as a noun (DI-gest) refers to a summary or collection - D-I-G-E-S-T. Digest as a verb (di-GEST) means to break down food.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'overlap' as a noun?
options: A) There is some overlap between the topics.
B) The circles will overlap.
C) These ideas overlap completely.
D) The schedules overlap on Tuesdays.
explanation: Overlap (O-ver-lap) as a noun means the area where things coincide - O-V-E-R-L-A-P. As a verb it means to extend over and cover.

questionText: The word 'insult' changes stress. Which sentence uses it as a verb?
options: A) Do not insult your classmates.
B) That remark was an insult.
C) The insult hurt her deeply.
D) He bore the insult silently.
explanation: Insult (in-SULT) as a verb means to offend - I-N-S-U-L-T. Insult (IN-sult) as a noun refers to an offensive remark.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'transfer' as a noun?
options: A) She requested a transfer to another school.
B) He will transfer the funds today.
C) Please transfer this data now.
D) They agreed to transfer ownership.
explanation: Transfer (TRANS-fer) as a noun means the act of moving - T-R-A-N-S-F-E-R. Transfer (trans-FER) as a verb means to move.

questionText: The word 'invalid' has two meanings. Which sentence uses it to mean not valid?
options: A) The ticket was invalid.
B) The invalid needed medical care.
C) She was an invalid after surgery.
D) He cared for an invalid.
explanation: Invalid (in-VAL-id) means not valid - I-N-V-A-L-I-D. Invalid (IN-va-lid) means a person with an illness.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'frequent' as a verb?
options: A) She frequents the library.
B) He is a frequent visitor.
C) Frequent storms hit the coast.
D) They make frequent mistakes.
explanation: Frequent (free-QUENT) as a verb means to visit often - F-R-E-Q-U-E-N-T. Frequent (FREE-kwent) as an adjective means happening often.

questionText: The word 'increase' changes stress. How is it stressed as a noun?
options: A) IN-crease
B) in-CREASE
C) IN-CREASE
D) in-crease
explanation: Increase as a noun stresses the first syllable - IN-crease. It means a rise or addition. As a verb it is in-CREASE.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'convert' as a noun?
options: A) He became a convert to the faith.
B) She will convert the data.
C) They plan to convert the building.
D) Convert this file to PDF.
explanation: Convert (CON-vert) as a noun means a person who has changed religion or belief - C-O-N-V-E-R-T. Convert (con-VERT) as a verb means to change.
